questions.q: If an artwork consists solely of perfect blue squares of the exact same size, it might look boring. To fix this, an artist adds a red circle and a green triangle. Which principle of design has been introduced?
questions.explain: Variety is the principle of design used to introduce differences, contrast, and change in an artwork. It prevents monotony and keeps the viewer visually engaged.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Art Fundamentals & Elements of Design
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Which statement best describes the relationship between 'Variety' and 'Harmony' in an artwork?
options: They are exactly the same concept.
They are opposing forces; one brings differences for interest, while the other brings similarities to unify the piece.
Harmony creates chaos, while Variety creates order.
Variety is only used in painting, and Harmony is only used in music.
questions.explain: Variety creates contrast and interest (preventing boredom), while Harmony ties everything together through similarities (preventing chaos). A successful artwork balances both principles.
